source.publication: 2025 NJ-1040 Instructions (with GIT-1 & 2 Retirement Income, January 2026, and njit6/njit7 web pages where named)
source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 16a, 17, 20a, 27, 28a, 28b, 29: Instr PDF p.10 and p.15 (Social Security not taxable), PDF p.22 line 28a (Line A, Line B and chart), PDF p.22 line 28b and PDF p.23 Worksheet D lines 1-9 with the Maximum Exclusion chart, PDF p.22 line 29; GIT-1 & 2 p.22-23; PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 70,400.00 (New Jersey public pension 40,000.00 + interest 6,000.00 + dividends 4,000.00 + taxable Social Security 20,400.00 (85% of 24,000.00: provisional income 50,000 + 12,000 = 62,000; 0.85 x (62,000 - 34,000) + 4,500 = 28,300, capped at 20,400)); federal taxable income = 70,400.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 54,650.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Social Security is exempt and not reported. Line 16a interest 6,000.00 + line 17 dividends 4,000.00 + line 20a pension 40,000.00 = line 27 total income 50,000.00 (projection: federal AGI 70,400.00 less taxable Social Security 20,400.00); measure 50,000.00, in the 0-100,000 band (keep share 1). Line 28a: age 63; Line A 40,000.00, Line B 75,000.00; lesser = 40,000.00. Worksheet D: line 1 maximum 75,000.00 - line 2 40,000.00 = line 3 35,000.00; lines 4-8 wages and business income 0.00 (not over 3,000); line 9 unclaimed exclusion 35,000.00 available, used against her remaining income of 10,000.00 (interest 6,000 + dividends 4,000), so line 28b = 10,000.00 (projection: room 75,000 - 40,000 = 35,000.00, covered interest and dividends 10,000.00, lesser 10,000.00). Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 50,000.00 - 40,000.00 - 10,000.00 = 0.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 1 (nobody is 65 or older, so no senior exemption) = 1,000.00; line 38 = 1,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 0.00 - 1,000.00 = 0.00 (not below zero). Line 43 tax on 0.00 = 0.00. No credits. State income tax = 0.00. The pension is noncontributory, so the New Jersey taxable amount (line 20a) equals the federal taxable amount and line 20b is empty. Line 29 is 0.00, below the 10,000 filing threshold, so no tax is due.
